approved: DRAFT - v2 plus the shop card text, waiting for the user
priorities: Exposure first: be seen by as many different agents as possible. Stock many categories in small quantities, watch what is selling right now (our own recent sales and what the market settled in the last hours, market.selling) and move stock toward it, and make the first deal with a new buyer an easy, good one, even at a small loss within the limits.
Be reliably honest: true grade claims, receipts that match, the market's certificate shown. Other agents remember the deals they had with us.
Buyer: maximise surplus on useful items. Read market prices, check certificates, shelf life and warranty, and be patient only when the surplus is large.
Learn: explore participants we have not traded with, and record everything; the next strategy is built from these records.
Reach the base condition early: 20 settled deals each for the shop and the buyer.
context: Round 3 has just opened and we have no Round 3 records yet: what sells, who buys, and what other shops charge are unknown.
The market lists 5,629 SKUs (4,311 food, 1,318 goods) in 140 demand categories.
Our week-07 shop was honest with 4.5+ stars but got only 0.7% of market visits, because its first prices were too high.

shop_card.description: gom31 Honest Shop: we only tell the truth. Every grade we state is the grade the unit has right now, the market's certificate comes with every unit that has one, and the receipt always matches the price we agreed. Groceries and goods. Ask for an item by SKU, category or name, then send a price; we answer with a counteroffer or a signed receipt.

experiment.hypothesis: H1: easy first prices and honest deals bring many different buyers and good stars, which later carry profit.
experiment.note: Thresholds are a starting point the user accepted on 2026-11-03, to be adjusted from the first results. v2 changes only the rollback threshold, 300,000 -> 500,000 (10% of the starting capital; about one full food stock thrown away). Selling below cost is not in losses.total; the brief shows it as unit_economics.seller.exposure_cost, with no threshold. The risk limits are a first guess too: the strategy agent proposes new values from the records and the user decides. Repeat-visit, star and sell-through metrics need the outer runtime's ledger collection (build step 5).
